title: Introduce wait-score slab redispatch and probabilistic starvation mitigation in continuous batcher
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduce wait-score slab buckets and redispatch queue for continuous batcher; new tuning knobs for starvation mitigation; conservative defaults. Observability: new metrics and dashboards.
description:
Motivation: Continuous batcher has edge cases where long-lived KV-pinned requests or heavy single-user tails can monopolize dispatch scheduling and cause starvation for short requests. Previous fixes (deadline windows, aging) reduced cases but we still see slippery fairness regressions under mixed workloads. This PR introduces a wait-score 'slab' bucketing approach plus an inexpensive redispatch slab to reduce tail-driven starvation while keeping scheduling overhead minimal.

What this PR changes (single-string description): - Add wait-score slab histogram: requests are scored by effective wait-time + penalty terms and placed into O(8) slabs instead of a full priority queue; slabs reduce contention and make redispatch cheaper. - Introduce a redispatch slab that holds recently-evicted or delayed requests and probabilistically re-injects them with jittered backoff to avoid synchronized storms. - Probabilistic starvation mitigation: a per-request decay token that increases chance of promotion for requests observed behind repeated dispatches; deterministic promotion path retained for strict deadlines. - KV pin detection hook: lightweight probe that marks requests touching long-term KV pins and biases them to the redispatch slab to avoid long-duration holds on hot lanes. - Timeout jitter window: jittered soft-timeouts to avoid thundering retransmit toward the scheduler at bucket boundaries. - Kernel hint plumbing: pipeline API accepts an optional hint (latency_sensitive|throughput_favored) used by the batcher to prefer compact batches with small latency-sensitive tokens; no model kernel changes here but this paves the way for per-batch kernel selection. - Observability: new metrics batcher.wait_score_slab_counts, scheduler.redispatch_injections, kv.pin_starvation_incidents and a dashboard template. - Config knobs: continuous.batch.wait_score_slab_count, continuous.batch.redispatch_fraction, continuous.batch.starvation_decay_ms, continuous.batch.timeout_jitter_ms. Defaults chosen conservatively to match current production tail numbers.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc referenced in Linear ENG-4512 - [x] Unit tests for slab placement and promotion - [x] Microbenchmarks for scheduling overhead - [x] E2E replay test showing improved 99th/99.9th percentiles on mixed workloads - [x] Observability dashboard PR (linked) - [x] Docs/CHANGELOG entry

Risk and rollout plan: Defaults are conservative (slab_count=8, redispatch_fraction=0.02). We will rollout as a progressive feature flag: 1) small internal canary (10% traffic), 2) cohort expand to 50% while watching scheduler.redispatch_injections and kv.pin_starvation_incidents, 3) full rollout if regressions are absent. Hot fallback: feature flag off reverts to previous queueing.

Notes: I intentionally avoided moving to a fully preemptive scheduler to keep the runtime lock-free paths and batching costs low. This change aims for <=1% CPU overhead at 8k qps while improving 99.9p by 15-35% in skewed KV workloads.

5 commits: initial slab bucket implementation; redispatch slab + jitter; KV pin probe and heuristic; add metrics + dashboards; tests and docs. Commit messages: 
- feat(scheduler): add wait-score slab buckets and placement logic
- feat(scheduler): implement redispatch slab with jittered backoff
- perf(kv): add small KV-pin probe to bias long-lived requests
- test(observability): add metrics and dashboard template
- fix(ci): address lint and race in e2e replay test

All commits signed and unit-tested locally.

review_conversation:
Jordan Kim: Curious about the synchronization cost of slab placement. Can we avoid atomics on the hot path?
Asha: We use per-worker slab lanes with eventual global merges; hot path does two relaxed atomics to increment slab counters. Microbenchmarks show ~0.25% overhead at 8k qps.
Riley Morgan: Please ensure the jitter distribution doesn't hide real SLO violations (i.e. don't push latency beyond client timeouts).
Asha: jitter window is soft and bounded by continuous.batch.timeout_jitter_ms (default 10ms), we added tests to prove no observable client timeout regressions in replay.
Samir Rao: Add an explicit e2e test for heavy KV-pin scenario to prevent regressions.
Asha: added tests/scheduler/test_redispatch_e2e.replay and a fixture in replay_tools.
CI bot: lint failed on first run (clang-format); author fixed style.
Riley Morgan: Approved after tests and small doc clarifications. Jordan: Approved with comment to watch redispatch_injections metric during rollout.
ci_summary:
Pipeline runs: linux-build (pass), unit-tests (pass after fix), integration-replay (pass), lint (fail -> fixed), e2e-replay (flaky -> deterministic after adding small sleep in fixture), perf-microbench (pass). One flaky test (test_replay_heavy_kv) caused rerun; root cause was test harness race and was fixed. Total CI time ~42m.
CI artifacts: scheduler_microbench_2026-02-18.html, e2e_replay_report_2026-02-19.json
perf_results: Microbenchmarks (internal replay harness): baseline vs this PR on mixed KV skew workload (100K requests, 10% heavy KV pins): - median latency: baseline 9.8ms -> PR 9.9ms (+1%) - 95p: baseline 17.3ms -> PR 15.1ms (-12.7%) - 99.9p: baseline 231ms -> PR 165ms (-28.6%) CPU overhead observed: +0.9% overall, scheduler CPU slice +3.4% but within headroom. End-to-end cost per token unchanged within noise. Observability replay shows drop in kv.pin_starvation_incidents by ~84%.
merge_status: Merged via squash-merge to main by Riley Morgan after approvals. Merge commit: feat(scheduler): wait-score slab + redispatch (squash). Post-merge actions: created rollout ticket ENG-4513-rollout and observability PR opened to add dashboard to tenant orgs.
notes_on_backward_compatibility: No API breaking changes. Added optional kernel hint field in batch metadata; server treats missing values as legacy behavior. Config defaults ensure parity with previous scheduling behavior unless feature flag enabled.
observability_changes: Added metrics: batcher.wait_score_slab_counts{slab=0..7}, scheduler.redispatch_injections, kv.pin_starvation_incidents, batcher.timeout_jitter_hist. Dashboard template at docs/observability/scheduler_waitscore_dash.yaml. Alerting recommendations: fire if redispatch_injections > 0.5% sustained or kv.pin_starvation_incidents > 10/min.
documentation: CHANGELOG updated with short note. Design notes in Linear ENG-4512 with diagrams. Added docs/observability and short README in src/serving/scheduler/README.md describing knobs and safe defaults.
rollback_instructions: Flip feature flag continuous.batch.waitscore_enabled=false or revert the deployment. If redispatch_metric spike is observed, rollback immediately and investigate backpressure. Also provided a small k8s job script to toggle feature flags across clusters.
test_plan: Unit tests added for slab placement and promotion. Integration replay verifies median/95/99.9p improvements. Canary rollout with telemetry checks, and a stress test (48h) on staging to ensure no memory growth from redispatch slab.
